title: Nigeria not giving up on World Cup hope, will appeal FIFA rejection of case against DR Congo
content:
The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) says it will appeal FIFA’s decision to reject its allegation that DR Congo fielded ineligible players in the World Cup play-off between the two nations.

DR Congo advanced to the inter-confederation play-offs after beating Nigeria on penalties in November in the second round of African qualifying. They are scheduled to play the winner of Jamaica vs. New Caledonia at the Estadio Akron in the Mexican city of Zapopan on March 31.

Nigeria subsequently filed a petition with FIFA, global football’s governing body, alleging “perceived fraud” in the supplying of passports that the NFF argues qualified “a number” of DR Congo players for the play-offs.

In a statement, the NFF said FIFA had rejected the protest but plans to appeal the decision.

“We have received the decision of the FIFA Disciplinary Committee on our petition, but we are not satisfied with the decision, which rejected our petition,” said NFF general secretary Mohammed Sanusi. “I want to assure Nigerians that the NFF has immediately commenced the process of appealing the decision.”

The Athletic has contacted FIFA and the Congolese Association Football Federation for comment.

The NFF’s argument centres around the principle of dual nationality. According to the UK government, DR Congo does not recognise dual nationality, with the only exception being if a child was born abroad and held the citizenship of the country where they were born. They must renounce this citizenship when they turn 21.

Sanusi claimed in December that “many” DR Congo players had other passports.

“The Congolese rules say you cannot have dual nationality,” Sanusi told reporters at the time. “There are so many of them that have European passports, some of them, French passports, some of them, Dutch passports. The rules are very clear.

“FIFA regulations say once you have the passport of your country, you are eligible. As far as we are concerned, they are eligible, that is why they are cleared by FIFA. But our contention is that FIFA was deceived into clearing them because it is not the responsibility of FIFA to make sure that the regulations of Congo are abided by.”

DR Congo won the play-off 4-3 on penalties after the game finished in a 1-1 draw. At full time, Nigeria head coach Eric Chelle alleged that DR Congo’s players were practicing “voodoo” during their penalty shootout victory. A representative of DR Congo denied Chelle’s claims when asked by The Athletic. Chelle later apologised for his comments.

Nigeria failed to qualify for the World Cup for the second tournament in a row, while DR Congo are seeking their second appearance at the competition. The only other time they qualified for the tournament was in 1974, when the country was known as Zaire, and lost all three of their games against Scotland, Yugoslavia and Brazil.
